clue.text: Lucky flier receives a medal

indicators.note: the bird takes the medal into its middle, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a jay is a bird, so a flier
MM is the Military Medal, a British award for bravery

explanation.surface: A pilot or bird has been fortunate enough to be decorated.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for fortunate, especially undeservedly so.

clue.text: Skips dessert to get car going

parts.note: to skip is to jump
a tart is a dessert

explanation.surface: Someone skips pudding in a hurry to drive off.
explanation.definitionFit: To start a vehicle with jump leads from another battery.

clue.text: Fly from pole to pole, it would be no big deal

definitions.text: Fly from pole to pole, it would be no big deal

parts.words: Fly from pole to pole, it would be no big deal
parts.note: an insect measured from one end to the other is tiny, so flying across it is nothing much

explanation.surface: Travelling from the North Pole to the South Pole would be easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like a verb of travel; it is the insect, and 'from pole to pole' is its length end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny biting insect, so something small and insignificant.

clue.text: Your chest is listened to by a houseman

indicators.note: listened to means we go by the sound of the words

parts.note: kist is a Scottish and northern word for a chest, so your chest is your kist

explanation.surface: A junior hospital doctor listens to a patient's chest.
explanation.walkthrough: A houseman is a junior hospital doctor, but here it is a member of a royal House; the Yorkists fought the Lancastrians in the Wars of the Roses.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of the royal House of York, so a man of that house.

clue.text: To punish players. I impose restriction

parts.note: the actors in a play are its cast
gating is confining a pupil or student to grounds, so gate is a restriction

explanation.surface: A coach decides to discipline the team by imposing a curfew.
explanation.walkthrough: To GATE a pupil is to confine them to school grounds, a British boarding-school punishment; 'impose' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to rebuke or chastise severely.

clue.text: Seasoning, some of which I'll incorporate

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cook says they will add some seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot pepper used as a spice.

clue.text: There's money in marketing magic

indicators.note: the money letter goes inside the marketing word

parts.note: selling is marketing
P is a penny, a coin

explanation.surface: There's profit to be made from magic in marketing.
explanation.definitionFit: Casting spells, enchantment.

clue.text: Provoke one to get new girlfriend

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a flame is a sweetheart

explanation.surface: Getting a new girlfriend is sure to stir up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To arouse or stir up strong feelings.

clue.text: Worker — after a year and a night abroad, he gets paid regular amounts

indicators.note: the worker comes after the year and the night in the answer

parts.note: an is French for year, the clue's abroad pointing to French
nuit is French for night, the clue's abroad pointing to French
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A labourer who works abroad gets regular wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' says both 'year' and 'night' are in French: AN and NUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: One who receives an annuity, a fixed yearly payment.

clue.text: Contemplating, for instance, adopting a Chinese principle

indicators.note: adopting means the example abbreviation takes the principle in

parts.note: EG is for instance
yin is the feminine principle in Chinese philosophy

explanation.surface: Considering taking up Chinese philosophy, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking at closely, regarding.

clue.text: Adapt to present day — get up about noon following the fashion

indicators.note: the risen piece comes after the fashion word, so it follows it in the answer

parts.note: the mode is the current fashion

indicators.note: the getting-up word wraps around the letter for noon

parts.note: to rise is to get up

explanation.surface: Advice to modernise: get out of bed late and keep up with trends.
explanation.definitionFit: To update something so it suits current times.

clue.text: Truffles perhaps give pleasure to soldier

parts.note: fun is enjoyment or pleasure
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Treating a soldier to delicacies like truffles.
explanation.definitionFit: Truffles are an example of mushroom-like organisms in this kingdom.

clue.text: Fish supplement sent back by chief in unfair argument

indicators.note: one turning signal sends both the fish and the postscript backwards together

parts.note: plaice is a flatfish
PS (postscript) is a supplement to a letter
leading means main or chief

explanation.surface: A complaint about a fish supplement being returned by the head chef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' reverses PLAICE + PS as one run, giving SPECIALP.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal term for one-sided argument that highlights favourable points and ignores the rest.

clue.text: Knowing statue got broken

indicators.note: a broken statue lies in pieces, so its letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A clever remark about a statue that was smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: shrewd, sharp-witted.

clue.text: Much exalted king, skilful and fair

indicators.note: exalted means raised up, so in a down clue the word is read upwards

parts.note: a lot means much
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the monarch
able means skilful

explanation.surface: A highly praised king who was talented and just.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exalted' lifts LOT so it reads TOL in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in the sense of reasonably good, passable.

clue.text: Stake fruit to make it earlier

parts.note: the ante is a stake in poker
a date is a fruit

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: support a fruit tree with a stake so it ripens earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign an earlier date to something, such as a document.

clue.text: Patient suffering, a creed nun cultivated

indicators.note: cultivated means worked over and changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nun's faith is grown through long patient suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Patient tolerance of hardship.

clue.text: Disrupting a film, the intermission

indicators.note: disrupting means throwing into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Interrupting a film is the purpose of the interval.
explanation.definitionFit: The break between two halves of a game.

clue.text: Finally caught by exotic animal's charm

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word caught
exotic means foreign or strange, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone caught by a strange beast's spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucky charm is an object thought to bring good fortune, an amulet.

clue.text: Set of cards where 10 turns up instead of one — that's fishy

indicators.note: instead of says one piece replaces another

parts.note: a suit is a set of cards, such as hearts
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: turns up means the letters are read upward in this down clue

parts.note: refers to 10-across, truffles perhaps; ceps are edible mushrooms

explanation.surface: A card game where the ten appears in place of the ace, which seems dodgy.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' refers to 10-across: CEPS are an example of those; 'turns up' makes SPEC, which goes 'instead of' I in SUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspect as an adjective means dubious, open to doubt.

clue.text: A group of soldiers, back in bed, dropped off

indicators.note: the turned soldiers sit inside the word bed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back means the soldiers' letters are read the other way

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: A squad of soldiers returned to their beds and fell asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TA into AT, which goes 'in' BED.
explanation.definitionFit: Abated means lessened or subsided, as a storm drops off.

clue.text: Bill overwhelmed by murderer in show

indicators.note: the bill is swallowed up by the murderer word around it

parts.note: a bravo is a hired assassin
an ad is a bill, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A poster crushed by a killer during a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a showy display of boldness.

clue.text: Disappointing finish causes upset

parts.note: off means below standard, disappointing
an end is a finish

explanation.surface: A poor ending to a match leaves fans upset.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend is to hurt someone's feelings.

clue.text: Resolution I'd offer the Arabs and similar people

indicators.note: resolution here means breaking down and resolving into parts, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A proposal to Arab negotiators offered as a resolution.
explanation.definitionFit: From the proverb about like-minded people flocking together.

clue.text: Pretend to travel up in public transport

indicators.note: the turned travel word goes inside the transport word

parts.note: a bus is public transport

indicators.note: up means the travel word reads upwards in this down entry

parts.note: to go is to travel

explanation.surface: Pretending to ride up town on a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretend as an adjective means fake, not genuine.

clue.text: Jack is in close

indicators.note: is goes inside the close word

parts.note: close weather is hot and humid

explanation.surface: A sailor is kept in confinement.
explanation.definitionFit: To jack up a car is to raise or lift it.

clue.text: Actor in part of wall

explanation.surface: An actor appears as part of a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Clark Gable was a Hollywood film star; a gable is the triangular upper end wall of a pitched roof.

clue.text: I/10 — that's about the proportion going over

indicators.note: the number word goes around the proportion

parts.note: ten is the number 10
a ratio is a proportion

explanation.surface: A fraction, one tenth, described as the proportion being exceeded.
explanation.definitionFit: Repetition: going over something again.

clue.text: A hitch involving leaf mould

parts.note: a leaf of paper is a sheet
to mould is to bend into shape

explanation.surface: A problem caused by leaf mould in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot used to join two ropes, a hitch being a kind of knot.

clue.text: Soldiers at first completely beyond the pale

indicators.note: the word for completely is placed at the front, ahead of the soldiers

parts.note: out means completely, as in out and out
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Troops who were utterly unacceptable from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means unconventional, eccentric, outside accepted bounds.
